decision: probed the machine for toolchain and model credentials before planning anything
why: did not want to design against assumptions about what was installed
evidence: powershell probe of node/npm/bun/git/gh/python and env vars
result: no node on PATH, no LLM key of any kind, git and gh and python present

decision: tested the gh token against GitHub Models instead of assuming it would work
why: whether a credential works is measurable, so measuring beat guessing
evidence: live call to models.github.ai catalog and inference endpoints
result: both returned HTTP 410, GitHub Models was retired 2026-07-30, path permanently closed

decision: found node was already installed rather than missing
why: winget said the package existed, so the real problem was a stale PATH not a missing install
evidence: winget list OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS, node --version after prepending the dir
result: node 24.19.0 and npm 11.17.0 work, every node command must prepend the winget portable dir

decision: treated the dev box and the production host as different hardware
why: dev here has no GPU at all, production is a 4090 with 24GB, so a GPU-dependent test suite would be unrunnable locally
evidence: Win32_VideoController shows only Hyper-V Video, nvidia-smi absent
result: engine tests must run against a deterministic fake DM, real model smoke-tested separately

decision: made a bootstrap commit on main so feature worktrees could exist
why: a brand new repo has no HEAD, and worktrees need one
result: main has a root commit, .worktrees/ is gitignored

decision: created the feature worktree and did all work there
why: house rule is that the primary checkout is never edited directly
result: worktree live, primary root resolves correctly from inside it

decision: built a model probe before designing the DM contract
why: the contract depends on whether a local model can be trusted to emit valid actions, and that is a number not an opinion
result: probe runs three decoding modes and validates against real engine invariants

decision: measured three decoding modes against a real local model
why: wanted the comparison against a baseline rather than just testing the mode I expected to win
evidence: probe output, 8 trials each on qwen2.5:3b-instruct
result: unconstrained 0/8, plain JSON mode 0/8, schema-constrained 8/8

decision: rejected plain JSON mode despite it parsing on every trial
why: it parsed 8/8 and was still wrong 8/8, emitting capital-N Narration and no intent at all
result: a parse-only gate would have scored it perfect, so the gate had to check shape not syntax

decision: split model failure into two classes and only claimed one was solved
why: constrained decoding fixes shape, it cannot stop a schema-valid action from being rules-illegal
result: engine still owns rules validation, that is now the only place model output can be rejected

decision: dropped the transpiler and test framework from the plan
why: node 24 runs .ts directly and node --test handles .ts, so ts-node and jest and vitest all earn nothing
evidence: ran a .ts file and a .ts test directly, both passed
result: API tier and engine tests need zero build tooling

decision: sent the DM contract to four competing designs instead of picking one
why: it is a one-way door, and a wrong call here means either a DM that hallucinates HP or a DM that cannot improvise
evidence: four background runners on claude-opus-5, gpt-5.6-sol, grok-4.5, gemini-3.8-flash
result: open

decision: pushed the probe result to the running candidates mid-flight
why: they were designing a parse-repair ladder for a problem the runtime already eliminates
result: all four acknowledged, still running

decision: took candidate 1 as the synthesis base
why: it was the only one that made illegal actions undecodable instead of merely rejected, by building the JSON schema per turn from live world state
result: open

decision: measured candidate 1's own open question instead of leaving it open
why: it flagged that long target enums might degrade choice quality, and that is measurable so it was not the operator's to answer
result: confirmed the risk is real and worse than expected

decision: found that enum validity stays perfect while enum correctness collapses
why: at 25 entities the model still always picked a valid target and picked the RIGHT one only 3 of 8 times, usually attacking an unarmed old woman
result: in-enum 24/24 across all sizes, correct 8/8 then 4/8 then 3/8

decision: made inReach scoping a load-bearing rule rather than a convenience
why: a generous target list is actively harmful and no validity metric would ever report it
evidence: brief.ts scopeCast in the synthesized design
result: open, needs a cap and a test enforcing it

decision: left the project uncatalogued at the operator's request
why: asked because it is a preference no experiment settles, and the answer was skip
result: worktree and branching rules still followed this session, nothing persists to the next

decision: synthesized the four candidates into one design package
why: candidate 1 was the base, with named grafts from the other three and re-prompting rejected outright
result: tsc --noEmit exits 0, verified independently not taken on trust

decision: cut the mint slots from 4 to 2 after the merge caught a hole in my own instruction
why: capping inReach at 6 still gave a decoder enum of 10 once mint slots were added, which is exactly the 4-of-8 condition I was trying to avoid
evidence: director.ts MAX_TARGET_ENUM derived from MAX_IN_REACH plus MINT_SLOTS
result: total enum bounded at 8 and derived rather than duplicated

decision: accepted the worker's refusal to force three outcomes into one union
why: rewrite and drop are per-effect and co-occur, soft-fail is a property of the whole turn, so one union would have had to lie
evidence: AdmissionReport and TurnResult in the package
result: my instruction was wrong and was corrected rather than worked around

decision: installed ollama and pulled a small model on the GPU-less box
why: every measurement in this trail depends on it, and the trail did not record where the numbers came from
result: serving on 11434, added retroactively during the self-audit

decision: my own audit grep reported a missing hostileDirector that was present all along
why: the pattern matched export const and export function but not export declare const, so the check was wrong not the delegate
result: false negative, logged because the same class of error is what this run kept hunting

decision: ran the mandatory cross-model review of this trail on a different model family
why: the work was done by claude-opus-5 so self-review could not catch its own blind spots
result: three checked findings all confirmed true

decision: SUPERSEDES the enum-degradation rows. the length effect does not exist
why: the reviewer found the conditions used different distractors. the attractor sat at index 5 so it was absent from the 3-entity case and present in the larger ones, which manufactured the trend
result: corrected run 6/8 3/8 3/8 4/8 6/8 for sizes 3 6 8 10 25, no trend

decision: MAX_IN_REACH 6 now has no evidence behind it and must be revisited
why: it was derived by interpolating a trend that turned out to be an artifact of my own experiment design
result: open, the cap is unjustified not necessarily wrong

decision: gave the unconstrained and json-mode baselines the field names they were never shown
why: the original comparison only told schema mode what shape to produce, so a baseline failure could have meant cannot comply or was never asked
result: not yet re-run, the fair-baseline number is still unknown

decision: closed the transport gap the reviewer flagged as most dangerous
why: both probes measured /api/generate while the design advertises /v1, so the guarantee might not have transferred
result: /v1 with response_format json_schema also 8/8, gap closed favourably

decision: built the runnable slice instead of generating a verification skill against unimplemented bodies
why: the create-verification-skill skill says to fix a non-running base first, and every body was still not implemented
result: 17 tests green with no GPU, tsc clean

decision: mutation tested every engine rule against only its own named test
why: a mutant killed by the full suite does not show the test named for the rule is the one that caught it
result: 7/7 killed, each by its own named test

decision: found a real bug by looking at a screenshot that every green check had missed
why: the player's own words never reached the transcript, because the client rendered them optimistically then replaced them with a server view that never stored them
result: fixed by putting the utterance in the event log, two regression tests added

decision: generated and then actually executed the verification skill
why: an unexecuted skill is a draft, so the take-a-turn recipe was run exactly as written
result: 6/6 assertions PASS, evidence survived cleanup

decision: SUPERSEDES the evidence paths in the two rows above. they point at evidence/ which was later moved
why: commit 9243244 relocated the kept artifacts and gitignored the scratch directory, which broke the pointers
result: paths corrected here rather than by editing history

decision: second cross-model review found the central claim was false in the shipped code
why: rulings were collected in a local array and turned into events by a trailing loop that three early returns jumped straight over
result: every dropped intent was ruled on and then silently discarded

decision: emitted rulings at the decision point instead of in a trailing loop
why: fixing the three early returns would have left the next early return free to reintroduce it, so the shape was the bug
result: drops and failed-roll rewrites now reach the log, two mutants prove it

decision: gave adjudicate a working world that absorbs its own events
why: a freshly minted NPC was only in the events array, so a lookup against the stale world returned undefined and it could never die
result: an NPC invented this turn can now be killed this turn

decision: added an engage op, because combat was unreachable
why: attack is undecodable during exploration by design and nothing anywhere transitioned into combat, so the game could never leave peace
result: combat is now reachable and still exits when the last foe falls

decision: derived minted ids from the world seed and event count
why: the old id used a module counter reset by restart and a timestamp that wraps every 28 minutes, so two sessions could collide and replay was not deterministic
result: same world mints the same id, different seeds do not collide

decision: expanded the mutation harness from 7 rules to 17
why: the reviewer pointed out that 7 of 7 sounded complete while damage capping, absent targets and combat exit had no mutant at all
result: the expanded run immediately exposed 3 stale anchors and 2 genuinely uncovered rules

decision: wrote the two tests the surviving mutants demanded
why: removing engage from the schema and removing the absent-target drop both left their tests passing, which means those rules were not covered
result: 17/17 mutants now killed by their own named test

decision: read the operator's real 10-turn session out of the event log
why: they asked whether the log could drive improvements, and it is far better evidence than any scenario I invented
evidence: data/portale.db, copied read-only so the live session was untouched
result: 10 turns produced zero rolls, zero damage, zero rulings

decision: found the log could not answer why
why: the design called refusals telemetry and then never recorded which op the DM chose, so the most important question was unanswerable
result: added a proposed event, never shown to the player

decision: built a replay probe over the real transcript instead of inventing test scenes
why: the defects only appeared in real play, so the real play is the test corpus
result: baseline reproduced it exactly, narrate_only 10 of 10 and combat intent 0 of 4

decision: moved op ahead of narration in the schema
why: constrained decoding emits fields in declaration order, so the model wrote hundreds of words of prose and then picked an op to match what it had already written
result: the narrate_only monoculture ended immediately

decision: gave out-of-character messages an op enum with one member
why: asking the model nicely did not work. the player typed I just told you I stabbed him in the eye, keep up, and was attacked for it, because the sentence is full of violence
result: starting a fight over a meta comment went from 2 of 2 to 0 of 2, and is now undecodable

decision: chose over-eager combat over dropped attacks when tempering engage
why: tempering to stop false positives reintroduced a dropped stabbing. an early fight can be talked down, an erased action is the original complaint
result: violence dropped back to 0 of 4 across two consecutive runs

decision: my own out-of-character heuristic was disarming a real action
why: the keep up pattern matched I tell the dockhand to keep up as we run, which would have silently cancelled a legitimate turn
result: pattern removed, the real utterance still matches on ending with DM

decision: the minted-id test was passing on timing rather than on the property
why: it compared two ids, and a clock-based id also compares equal inside one millisecond and unequal across a tick, so it survived a Date.now mutant
result: rewritten to assert the id begins with the world seed, mutant now dies

decision: made engage resolve the blow that started the fight
why: driving the live model showed it entering combat and then discarding the stab, so the DM narrated a wound the world never took. that is the original bug wearing a different hat
evidence: rules.ts engage falls through to resolution
result: a roll and damage now happen on the turn combat begins

decision: told the DM to narrate the attempt and never the result
why: it wrote the dagger piercing her eye on a turn the roll then failed, so the prose and the die openly contradicted each other
evidence: director.ts narration rules with a wrong and right example
result: decided-the-outcome went from routine to 1 of 10

decision: raised the repetition penalties after the narration fix made repetition worse
why: a narrower brief leaves fewer ways to open a sentence, so constraining the prose pushed repeats from 1 of 10 to 5 of 10
result: back to 1 of 10, and op quality rose to 9 of 10 at the same time

decision: checked the dice before fixing them, and there was nothing to fix
why: three critical misses in a row looked like a broken generator, but 40000 rolls came out uniform at min 1904 max 2099
result: the repeats were my display window plus seq 2 and seq 6 both mapping to face 1 under seed 777

decision: scrubbed bookkeeping tokens out of narration at the boundary
why: the live DM opened a narration with ~new3 introduces, naming a slot that does not exist. asking it not to is necessary and not sufficient
result: the engine now replaces ids with names and slot tokens with someone

decision: my first scrub only covered the two declared slots and let the invented one through
why: the model wrote ~new3 and MINT_SLOTS only lists ~new1 and ~new2, so the test I had just written failed on the real input
evidence: rules.ts regex over any slot-shaped token
result: 34 tests, 23 of 23 mutants

decision: found the HTTP layer had no tests at all
why: unit tests never touch HTTP and the browser harness goes through the UI, so routing, status codes, the in-flight guard and traversal were unverified
result: 21 API tests added

decision: split the server into a constructible app and a thin entry
why: it built everything at module scope and listened on import, so nothing could test it in process
result: tests now build a real server on an ephemeral port with a scripted DM

decision: added a typed client and a CLI so the API can be driven without a browser
why: the operator asked for a direct line to the server, and a raw escape hatch is what makes status codes assertable
result: smoke passes 10 checks and exits non-zero on failure

decision: two of my own new API tests were passing for the wrong reason
why: the traversal test used a path with no file behind it so it 404d either way, and the body-limit test sent an oversized utterance that the length check caught first
result: fixed with a real canary file and short-utterance padding, 30 of 30 mutants now die

decision: fixed a libuv assertion on shutdown
why: closing the database inside the server close callback tore down a handle that was still closing
result: CLI now exits cleanly with the right code

decision: the live pass caught drift I had just written into the map
why: I added an out-of-character recipe that cannot work under the scripted DM, because that director never reads the schema the guard collapses
result: marked live-model-only and re-proved against the real model, no new roll added
